name: True Myelomeningocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Myelomeningocele

criteria.description: Presence of a protruding spinal sac containing meninges and spinal cord tissue
Neurological deficits below the lesion level including lower limb weakness or paralysis
MRI or ultrasound evidence of spinal cord and meningeal herniation through vertebral defect
Associated hydrocephalus detected clinically or radiologically

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a protruding spinal sac with spinal cord tissue confirmed by imaging and neurological deficits consistent with lesion level
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; prenatal ultrasound can detect the lesion antenatally.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visible spinal meningeal and neural tissue sac protrusion
pathognomonic.notes: Typically located in the lumbosacral region

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lower limb paralysis or severe paresis below lesion level

searchTerms: bladder control issues from nerve damage
brain tissue herniation at skull base

occasional.notes: Due to repeated exposure during surgeries

rare.symptomName: Respiratory complications due to thoracic involvement
searchTerms: lung complications due to chest involvement

laboratory: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein in maternal serum during pregnancy
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing spinal defect with protruding sac
MRI demonstrating spinal cord herniation and associated Chiari II malformation
CT scan showing bony vertebral defects
genetic: No specific genetic mutation; multifactorial etiology with folate metabolism involvement
other: Physical examination revealing open spinal defect with exposed neural tissue

distinguishingFeatures: No visible spinal sac or exposed neural tissue
Usually asymptomatic or mild neurological signs
Protruding sac contains meninges only without neural tissue
Less severe neurological deficits compared to myelomeningocele

redFlags: Rapidly increasing head circumference indicating hydrocephalus
Signs of infection at the spinal lesion site
Progressive neurological deterioration or new onset paralysis
references: Winkelman MD, et al. Myelomeningocele: Clinical features and management. UpToDate. 2024.
Adzick NS. Fetal surgery for myelomeningocele. Semin Fetal Neonatal Med. 2020.
